FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: potjevleesch
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: four white meats stacked into a terrine and cooked in {2_plur} with vinegar, then set to jelly in the cold. Eaten cold, with hot chips: that is the whole point of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hochepot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a pot-au-feu of the North, into which go the cuts nobody wants — tail, ear, trotter — with {1_coll} and {2_coll}. Hochepot: the pot that gets shaken.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: welsh rarebit
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted with {1_plur} and mustard, poured over a slice of bread and {2_coll}, then browned. A fried egg on top if you want the full version.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: leek flamiche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted in {2_plur} without colour, shut between two sheets of pastry and baked until the top gilds. Picard, and with no cream at all in the original.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: maroilles tart
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a risen dough covered with {0_adj} in slivers and {2_adj}, baked until the whole thing bubbles. The smell carries three rooms; the taste is milder than it lets you believe.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: herring with potatoes in oil
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: smoked fillets marinated in {2_plur} with onion and bay, over warm {1_coll} cut into rounds, which drink up the scented oil.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: caghuse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a wheel of {0_adj} cooked under a lid on a bed of {1_adj}, without a drop of water — the juice comes from the meat and the onions alone. Eaten cold the next day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pigs' trotters Sainte-Menehould
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: trotters poached for forty hours, until the bones turn tender and are eaten along with the rest, then crumbed and grilled. Louis XVI is said to have stopped for them during his flight, which delayed him.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: eel in green sauce
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: lengths of eel poached in white {2_plur} in a mass of green herbs — sorrel, watercress, spinach — until the sauce takes their colour. Served cold.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sole normande
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached in cider, garnished with {1_plur} and mushrooms, the sauce reduced and mounted with {2_plur}. One of the oldest bourgeois recipes still served.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: marmite dieppoise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: several fish and {1_coll} poached separately and only then brought together in a broth creamed with cider. Every flesh has its own cooking time: put them all in at once and the whole thing is lost.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mussels in cream
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} opened over a high flame in {2_plur}, the liquor they give up strained of its sand then reduced and bound with {1_plur}, and poured back over them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: duck à la rouennaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a bird smothered rather than bled, so as to keep its blood, roasted rare; the carcass is then pressed and the juice bound with the liver and red {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: black pudding with apples
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a black pudding pricked with a fork and fried gently — too fierce a heat and it bursts — with {2_coll} caramelised in butter. The sugar of the fruit cuts the iron of the blood.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: baked camembert
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole box of {0_adj} scored in a cross, stuck with {2_plur} and put into the oven in its own wood until it runs. Bread is dipped into it until there is nothing left.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: omelette de la Mère Poulard
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beaten very long with a whisk, until they foam like a soufflé, and cooked in {1_plur} in a long-handled pan over a wood fire. The exact recipe was never given away.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: lobster à l'armoricaine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cut up alive and seared in its own shell, flamed with cognac, stewed with {1_plur} and white {2_plur}, the sauce thickened with the coral. Armoricaine or américaine: the quarrel has run for a century.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: scallops à la bretonne
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} put back into its shell under garlic and parsley and breadcrumbs in {2_plur}, run under the grill for two minutes. Any longer and it turns to rubber.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: galette-saucisse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a grilled sausage rolled in a cold {0_adj} galette, and nothing else — mustard is tolerated, ketchup is disputed. Eaten standing, at the match or at the market.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed clams
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} opened and covered with a butter worked with {1_plur} and parsley, put into the oven until the butter bubbles up and runs over the edge.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: stuffed spider crab
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} picked out patiently, mixed with its own coral and the yolks of hard-boiled {1_adj}, then packed back into the emptied shell. An hour of work for ten minutes of eating.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pike-perch with beurre blanc
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a river fish poached, served under an emulsion of {2_adj} reduced in white wine, into which cold {1_coll} is worked piece by piece. The sauce splits at the first excess of heat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mogettes with ham
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: white Vendée {0_coll} cooked in barely trembling water with {2_coll}, half crushed to thicken their own broth, and served with a slice of {1_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rillettes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked five hours in {1_coll} until it falls apart, pulled with a fork and never ground, then pressed into a pot under a layer of fat that keeps it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Easter pâté
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a stuffing of {0_adj} shut inside a pastry, with whole hard-boiled eggs lined up down the middle so that a yellow disc appears in every slice.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poulet en barbouille
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} stewed in wine, the sauce thickened with the bird's own blood and liver. Barbouille, for what it leaves on the chin of whoever eats it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: chicken with morels
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} from the Jura and dried {1_coll} swollen back up in water — that soaking water, strained, is worth a stock — the sauce enriched with mountain {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: Morteau sausage with lentils
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a sausage smoked over resinous wood, poached without ever being allowed to boil, on {1_coll} stewed with {2_plur} stuck with cloves.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: hot mont d'or
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a whole box of {0_adj} pierced through, doused with white {1_plur} and garlic, put into the oven inside its spruce hoop until it turns liquid. Eaten with a spoon, with {2_coll} in their skins.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pâté lorrain
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cut by knife and marinated two days in white {2_plur}, shut inside a narrow puff pastry. Eaten warm, never scalding.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: potée lorraine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and the roots of winter stewed together with smoked and salted {1_coll}. The broth is served first, over bread; the meats come afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rabbit with mirabelles
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} coloured in {2_plur}, flamed with eau-de-vie and stewed with yellow {1_coll} that fall apart and sweeten the sauce without anything being added.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: quenelles sauce Nantua
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a stuffing of {0_adj} mounted with {1_plur} and panade, shaped with a spoon and poached, then swollen in the oven under a pink sauce of crayfish and {2_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: salade lyonnaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: bitter frisée, {2_coll} fried in the pan, croutons rubbed with garlic and a poached egg set over the top. You break the yolk and it becomes the dressing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poularde demi-deuil
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a fowl under whose skin black slivers of {1_adj} have been slid, poached whole in a broth of bones. The black on the white is what earns it its name: half-mourning.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tripe à la lyonnaise
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked ahead, cut into strips and fried in {2_plur} until the edges crisp, with {1_coll} turned golden and a splash of vinegar at the end.
